newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Historic Taiwan Strait crossing on Friday-HK paper.
newsitem.headline: Historic Taiwan Strait crossing on Friday-HK paper.

text.p: The first ship to sail directly from China to Taiwan in 48 years is expected to make the historic trip on Friday, a Hong Kong newspaper said on Thursday.
The South China Morning Post quoted shipping sources as saying Sheng Da, owned by China's Xiamen Harvest Shipping Co, would make the voyage.
However, officials from Taiwan and China refused to reveal information about the crossing, the English-language paper said.
It said the container vessel was scheduled to leave Xiamen's Haitian port and arrive in Kaohsiung harbour later on Friday.
The Sheng Da is one of four ships from five mainland China sea-freight firms which Taiwan recently approved to sail directly into Kaohsiung from China, it said.

China regards Taiwan as a renegade province and refuses to recognise the "Republic of China" government that has ruled the Nationalist redoubt since losing the mainland in a civil war in 1949 and fleeing to the island.
Direct shipping Links since that time have been banned.
Nationalist-ruled Taiwan denies that the long-forbidden crossings are direct links because mainland cargoes will not be allowed to enter Taiwan customs.
Rather, they can only be processed at what Taiwan is calling an "offshore transshipment centre" for onward passage to third countries.
